rule: These are proposals, not decisions. substance_equivalence_reviewed_v1 records who decided and on what evidence, so nothing here may be inserted under a review identifier until a person actually reviews it. A base-to-salt mapping asserts that the strength on the label means the same quantity in both, which is a dosing claim.
evidenceBasis: Archived SmPC sections in dose_source_sections_v3. A proposal is only source_proven when the archived section names the salt itself, and it is anchored on the section sha256 rather than the snapshot id, because snapshot identity is not stable across fetches.

proposals.quote: Adults: One 100 mg diclofenac sodium prolonged-release tablet daily
proposals.note: Strength, salt and release form all match, and the salt is named by the archived section rather than inferred. The form check matters here: the same 100 mg also exists as suppository, modified-release and gastro-resistant products, and a prolonged-release rule must not bind to those.
proposals.anchorNote: Anchored on the section sha256, not on snapshot_id. Snapshot identity is fetch-derived and changes on every archive run even when the document does not; see data/drx-snapshot-identity-instability-v1.json.

blockedProposals.why: Sections 4.1 and 4.2 never name the salt. The strength exists in the registry under bisoprololfumarate, but whether the SmPC's 10 mg is 10 mg of fumarate or of base is declared in section 2, which is now storable and parseable but has not been fetched yet.
Section 4.2 says only '1 tablet (10 mg) once daily'. The salt is never named in the archived sections. Section 2 would name it, but has not been fetched yet.
The archived sections never name the salt, and section 2 has not been fetched yet. Microgram dosing makes an unproven base-to-salt assumption particularly unsafe here.

pipelineGap.finding: The salt and strength basis of a medicine is declared in SmPC section 2 (qualitative and quantitative composition). Both layers that blocked reaching it are now open.
pipelineGap.parserLayer: RESOLVED: lib/smpc-parser.js gained extractCompositionSection. It is deliberately separate from SECTION_TITLES so clinicalSectionCoverage stays a ratio over the nine clinical sections, and it terminates at section 3 or 4 so section 2 cannot swallow section 3.
pipelineGap.schemaLayer: RESOLVED: migration 20260829213000_drx_v3_allow_composition_section widened dose_source_sections_v3.section_code to ^(?:2|4\.[1-9])$. Storage widened only - dose_rules_v3.source_section and both adjustment tables still check source_section = '4.2', so a rule can never cite section 2 as its dosing source.
pipelineGap.consequence: Storage and parsing are ready. The three unproven mappings stay unproven until the archive workflow is rerun so section 2 is actually fetched, hashed into the attestation and loaded. Nothing can be promoted before that: the evidence does not exist in the database yet.
pipelineGap.doNot: Do not close these by assuming the usual convention. The convention is usually right, which is exactly what makes an unchecked assumption here easy to miss and dangerous when wrong.
